key_insight: Specialized continued pretraining (LLaMat) enables smaller, domain-tuned LLMs to outperform larger general-purpose models in materials science. Excessive upstream pretraining (e.g., LLaMA-3) can reduce a model's ability to adapt to new scientific domains compared with less-extensively pretrained bases (e.g., LLaMA-2).
problem_solved: How to build efficient, high-performing LLMs for materials-research tasks and understand the trade-offs of continued pretraining versus model size and upstream pretraining extent.
method: Curated materials-science corpora and applied continued pretraining to create the LLaMat family across multiple base sizes.
Benchmarking LLaMat against larger general LLMs on domain-specific tasks and metrics to compare performance per parameter and data efficiency.
Controlled experiments analyzing adaptability: comparing effects of varying amounts of upstream pretraining (LLaMA-2 vs LLaMA-3) on ability to learn scientific domain data.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building resource-efficient, domain-specialized LLMs and highlights that more upstream pretraining is not always better for downstream scientific adaptation—crucial guidance for model selection and pretraining budgets in applied ML.
visual_elements: Performance vs model size chart showing LLaMat small/medium models outperforming larger general LLMs on materials benchmarks.
Adaptability curve: x-axis = amount of upstream pretraining, y-axis = downstream domain adaptation performance (illustrate LLaMA-2 vs LLaMA-3 trajectories).
Training pipeline diagram: data curation → continued pretraining → fine-tuning → evaluation (icons for corpora, compute, metrics).
Benchmark heatmap or bar chart comparing task-level scores (e.g., property prediction, literature QA, synthesis planning) across models.
paper_title: A family of large language models for materials research with insights into model adaptability in continued pretraining
paper_authors: Dhruv Ahlawat, Vaibhav Mishra, Somaditya Singh, Mohd Zaki, Vaibhav Bihani
